items.title: Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council
items.description: Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here . Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide. US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed. Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure. Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty. Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise. Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days. In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar. Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment. On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro. Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain. Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks. RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda. Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr. And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations. Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary. The government plans to put its internal political dialogue on the New York agenda. The process, now being hurried in Khartoum, is to be presented as nationally owned, with international actors there to support and facilitate rather than dictate its agenda or outcome. But a political source close to the dialogue said New York will test the international response to a process whose current, state-curated form is already being rejected by parts of the civilian political camp. Sudanese political and civilian forces, opposed to both the war and a military-led political process, rejected Burhan’s call for a dialogue, saying that any process launched while fighting continues — and conducted under military control — would reproduce the wartime balance of power rather than help end it. The collective rejection came at the end of consultative meetings held in Addis Ababa on Saturday and Sunday. *** Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns The RSF convoy that was struck by the military, August 26. Courtesy: @AbedaMoham6183 on X A fleet of military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of RSF combat vehicles, fuel trucks and military supply vehicles inside Chad on August 20, about 78 kilometers from the Sudanese border, a military source told Mada Masr. Chad said the strike on its territory threatened its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to urge restraint and dialogue to avert a regional escalation. According to the military source, the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya and was preparing to move into Darfur through Chad. The source said its objective was to reinforce RSF positions and participate in attacks on military-held areas in North Darfur and West Darfur, while helping the paramilitary group halt recent military advances on fronts in North Kordofan. One of the convoy’s immediate targets, according to the source, was Tina, the strategic border town in North Darfur and one of the last military-held pockets in the region. A second military source said that after the strike inside Chad, RSF fighters scattered. The military’s air operations room relayed their locations to the joint force of military-allied armed movements operating on the ground, and they moved to surround the fighters, the source added, saying the men had been wandering through the desert on foot. Some of the fighters managed to reach the Chadian town of Um Jaras in dire condition, according to the source. Videos released by fighters from the joint force showed dozens of captured RSF fighters in poor condition, apparently weakened by thirst and hunger. The joint force of military-allied armed movements said it destroyed 49 combat vehicles during an operation “in the desert axis,” captured 30 others and seized batteries used for operating drones, while detaining 70 RSF fighters. The first military source said the RSF has been seeking to establish new supply routes from southeastern Libya through Chadian territory and into North Darfur’s Wadi Howar to evade military ambushes and sustained strikes along its main supply route through the Sudan-Libya-Egypt border triangle. In a statement on Saturday, the Chadian armed forces said aircraft and drones believed to belong to the Sudanese military, or forces supporting it, attacked a convoy inside its eastern Ennedi region. The Chadian military placed all its units on maximum alert in anticipation of further field developments and said it reserved the right to take measures necessary to defend the country’s sovereignty. The Sudanese military has yet to comment. AU Commission Chair Mahmoud Ali Youssouf expressed deep concern over the incident and reaffirmed the AU’s commitment to the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of its member states and the inviolability of their borders. In a statement issued Wednesday, Youssouf called on all parties to “exercise utmost restraint, refrain from any action likely to heighten tensions between neighbouring States, and take all necessary measures to prevent the conflict in Sudan from extending beyond the country’s borders.” He also called for dialogue and cooperation among regional states to prevent cross-border incidents and reduce the risk of regional escalation, saying he was ready to support any initiative by the countries concerned aimed at de-escalation. US Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos said on Thursday that he held a call with Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Deby, where they discussed the military strike. “We […] underscored our deep concern about the war in Sudan spilling across its borders, fueling further escalation, and threatening regional peace and stability. External financial and military support to the warring parties must stop,” Boulos said. Military commander Mohamed Adam Kash, who heads the Sudan Liberation Movement, led by Darfur Governor Minni Arko Minnawi in North Darfur, denied that Sudan breached Chad’s borders. Speaking to Mada Masr, he insisted that Sudanese forces engaged the RSF inside Sudanese territory and that “there was no indication they crossed into Chadian airspace.” Kash said the force destroyed during the operation sought to enter through Wadi Howar and included large numbers of foreign fighters who knew little about Sudan or its geography. Many became scattered across the desert and were captured, he added. Kash called on Chad and other neighboring countries not to allow their borders to be used by convoys carrying mercenaries and military equipment intended for what he described as “attacks on Sudanese civilians.” He said supply routes to the RSF remain open along Sudan’s borders with South Sudan, Libya, Chad and Ethiopia, describing this as a violation of good-neighborly relations and respect for Sudanese sovereignty. The Sudan-Chad border stretches across a vast area and cannot be sealed or controlled by either side alone, Kash said. Unless Chad cooperates as a neighboring state, he stressed, the border will remain open to the movement of weapons and military equipment. *** RSF builds up forces in preparation for North Kordofan offensive More than 400 RSF combat vehicles carrying troops and weapons have been assembled in West Kordofan as the paramilitary group prepares for an operation against areas in North Kordofan it recently lost to the military, according to a field source in the military-aligned mobilized civilian brigades. The vehicles are being concentrated in Nuhud and the towns of Ghobeish and Laeet, the source told Mada Masr. They are arriving from Darfur in small groups, sometimes just five vehicles at a time, to reduce the risk of detection and attack by the military’s air force, they added. The buildup coincides with tighter restrictions in Nuhud. The RSF shut down all public markets and cut Starlink satellite communications there on Wednesday, according to the Dar Hamar emergency room. The emergency room said the measures were imposed as residents and displaced people were already facing difficult living conditions and relying heavily on satellite communications to contact relatives, receive money transfers and manage basic needs. It warned that the shutdown could amount to a commercial blockade and further restrict civilian life, calling for urgent intervention by regional and international humanitarian organizations to pressure the RSF to halt the measures and ensure continued access to essential services and communications. *** Military repels SPLM-N assault in strategic locality in South Kordofan The military repelled an attack by SPLM-N (Hilu) on the Damra area, about two kilometers outside the town of Abbasiya Tagali, South Kordofan. The attack began with intense artillery fire targeting military defenses, followed by a ground assault that was repelled by troops from the 10th Infantry Division, inflicting heavy losses on the attacking force, a field source in the military told Mada Masr. Security conditions in the Abbadiya Tagali locality have since returned to normal, the source said. The locality lies in the eastern mountains of South Kordofan and is defended by the 10th Infantry Division, which is headquartered in Abu Gebeiha. The locality links between the northern and southern parts of South Kordofan and gives the military control over key routes that influence the movement of troops and civilians in the area. *** Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership Otoro fighters seize an SPLM-N (al-Hilu) military vehicle during their incursion into Kauda in South Kordofan, August 23. Courtesy: Yasin Ahmed on X After weeks of fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the SPLM-N (Hilu) has failed to keep the conflict away from Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan. The Otoro tribe’s fighters returned to the town this week, days after SPLM-N forces had retaken it. The latest fighting and an intervention by RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo have pushed some Otoro groups to move beyond demands for greater representation in the SPLM-N’s institutions and call for Hilu’s removal, while seeking to build a broader alliance across the Nuba Mountains around the movement’s leadership and future, two Otoro tribal leaders told Mada Masr. According to a former military source in the SPLM-N, Otoro fighters had established a foothold in parts of Kauda in clashes with the movement during the first week of August. When SPLM-N forces moved in to contain the fighting, some Otoro fighters withdrew from their positions, while others remained in place, leaving the two sides deployed in overlapping areas both inside the town and in its surroundings. The movement treated the situation as one that could be resolved gradually, the source said, with its forces working to reclaim positions without immediately seeking to clear the Otoro fighters from the town altogether. But between August 15 and 17, the SPLM-N shifted from containment to direct offensive, sending reinforcements into Kauda and advancing on the remaining Otoro positions. The operation was aimed at ending the patchwork of control that had emerged inside the town and restoring the movement’s control over its institutions and military sites, the source said. By August 18, SPLM-N forces had retaken Kauda, according to four Otoro civilian fighters in and around the town. They said the movement pushed remaining Otoro fighters out of positions they still held and redeployed forces around key institutions and facilities, while Otoro fighters withdrew toward areas on the town’s outskirts. The former military source said Otoro fighters continued to operate in the areas near Kauda, prompting the SPLM-N to redistribute its forces and military positions after taking control. Some headquarters and sensitive sites were moved outside Kauda as a precaution against renewed fighting, while some units remained inside to secure government institutions and the main roads. The arrangement was followed by an attempt to stop the fighting through mediation. On August 20, the SPLM-N announced a halt to hostilities in Kauda and Heiban in response to what it said was an initiative put forward by Hemedti to end the fighting in the region. A political source in the movement said the decision was intended to make room for social mediation and prevent the conflict from escalating again after the SPLM-N had retaken Kauda. For some in the Otoro, however, the initiative was seen as an attempt by the RSF to intervene in a dispute that is specific to the Nuba Mountains in order to expand its influence in the region, particularly amid objections from some tribal groups to the SPLM-N leadership’s alliance with the RSF on the battlefield, and in the Tasis government in western Sudan, an Otoro member told Mada Masr. Within hours of the announcement, Otoro fighters accused SPLM-N forces of shelling their positions around Kauda with artillery, according to a second Otoro member. The source said the shelling effectively brought the ceasefire to an end. The SPLM-N denied the claim. A political source informed of the contacts between the two sides said the truce had been fragile from the outset, with SPLM-N and Otoro forces still deployed in the same area and no clear arrangements for separating the forces or determining where they would withdraw. The unresolved military presence around Kauda soon reversed the movement’s gains. Between August 21 and 24, Otoro fighters returned to parts of the town, according to the former military source, taking advantage of the SPLM-N’s redistribution of forces and the relocation of some headquarters outside Kauda. The fighters moved toward the town from areas in Heiban locality, the source said, drawing on their continued presence in the wider area to retake positions they had lost on August 18. A current SPLM-N military source said movement forces remained in parts of Kauda and that the developments did not amount to a complete withdrawal from the town. The four Otoro fighters likewise said SPLM-N forces remained positioned inside Kauda even as Otoro fighters returned to other areas, leaving the town as it was under overlapping control rather than a clear, stable control of either side. The recent fighting and the RSF leadership interference have begun to change the nature of the Otoro’s demands, a tribal leader informed of the discussions among Otoro groups told Mada Masr. The dispute started years earlier over the SPLM-N’s efforts to redraw administrative boundaries in areas under its control and redefine tribal landholdings across the Nuba Mountains. In recent months, the Otoro’s demands had expanded from opposition to encroachment on their ancestral lands to include greater representation in the movement’s civilian and military institutions. But after the latest round of fighting, the tribal leader said, some segments of the tribe were increasingly framing the dispute as a question of the movement’s leadership itself and its management of the Nuba Mountains, culminating in calls for Hilu to leave his position. By August 24 and 25, some Otoro groups were moving toward an approach that would take the dispute beyond direct negotiations with the movement’s leadership. A second Otoro tribal leader said some were seeking to build a broader alliance across the Nuba Mountains through the Nuba Mountains Liberation Council, an existing political and organizational framework inside the movement tasked with representing the region’s constituent communities. The council, they said, could bring together social, military and political forces that believe the region’s administration requires broader representation than the circle around Hilu. The aim is to shift the debate from the Otoro issue alone to the future of political power in the Nuba Mountains, they added. The former SPLM-N military source said the demand for Hilu’s departure represents the most difficult stage of the crisis so far. Land boundaries can be negotiated, as can arrangements for representation within the movement’s institutions, the source said. But changing the leadership would open a much broader debate over the movement’s political and military structure, its leadership council and institutions built over decades of war and self-rule in the Nuba Mountains. The Otoro tribe’s ability to gain the upper hand in Kauda, even temporarily, has also given them greater leverage, the source said, because of the town’s symbolic importance as the center of the movement’s political legitimacy. A political source close to the SPLM-N leadership said the call for Hilu’s removal represented an attempt to alter the movement from outside its established institutions. The source warned that allowing local constituencies to use force to effect leadership changes could create a precedent that would further undermine the movement’s internal cohesion. *** US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos gives a statement at a UN Security Council meeting on Sudan and South Sudan, August 24. Courtesy: UN Web TV The UN Security Council met on Monday for an open briefing on Sudan — a session that turned into a diplomatic showdown over a US proposal to expand the arms embargo currently imposed on Darfur to cover all of Sudan. US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos presented the draft resolution, having first raised the idea at a Security Council session in June . The proposal builds on a sanctions regime established by the council under Resolution 1591 in 2005, which imposed an arms embargo on parties to the Darfur conflict alongside individual measures including travel bans and asset freezes. The regime is due to expire on September 12 unless it is renewed or amended. Denmark, which holds the council presidency this August, had requested the meeting to discuss the protection of civilians and the humanitarian consequences of the war. Senior UN officials told the council that the escalation in the war has deepened the humanitarian crisis and raised concerns over further mass atrocities and the risk of wider regional spillover. Rosemary DiCarlo, the UN under-secretary-general for political and peacebuilding affairs, said drones used by both warring parties have repeatedly struck markets, schools, fuel stations and water infrastructure. The UN has recorded 1,400 civilian deaths in the first half of the year, with more than 1,100 attributed to drone strikes, UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher told the council. Boulos used the figures on drone casualties to make the case for the US proposal, saying drone strikes by both sides continued to hit civilians and civilian infrastructure. The draft would extend the existing Darfur arms embargo to all of Sudan and explicitly include drones and their associated systems and technologies, while expanding the Sudan sanctions panel and strengthening its cooperation with sanctions teams in the region to track the networks supplying and financing the warring parties. Boulos said the measure was intended to address the reality of the current war, particularly the outside military support that has helped prolong the fighting, and to push the parties toward a political track. The proposed steps, he said, were not designed to tilt the military balance toward either side, but to apply pressure on both simultaneously. “Nor do these measures seek to create or imply equivalence among the conflict parties beyond the fact that all must pursue peace and bear the burdens of accountability,” he said. Boulos nevertheless said “the brutality of the war waged by the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces has discredited their claims to be legitimate governors of the Sudanese people.” France and the UK supported extending the arms embargo across Sudan, while Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen called for the International Criminal Court’s jurisdiction to cover the entire country. Sudan’s permanent representative to the UN Al-Harith Idriss during the meeting, August 24. Courtesy: UN Web TV Sudan rejected the US proposal outright. Al-Harith Idriss, Sudan’s permanent representative to the UN, said extending the embargo nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia” by subjecting them to the same restrictions. He described the proposal as an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty and said it ignored the “legal differences between the parties.” Idriss said Sudan supported a “technical extension” of the existing sanctions regime, but not the broader change proposed by Washington. He called instead for the council to focus on enforcing the current measures and strengthening monitoring of the external networks supplying weapons and drones to the warring parties. The Sudanese diplomatic stand in New York came as Burhan said in Khartoum that potential sanctions would not alter the military’s position or its ability to continue fighting. Speaking at the graduation ceremony of police officers in the capital on Monday, Burhan insisted, “What is being said about the possibility of imposing sanctions on Sudan will not affect us.” Russia and China, two of the council’s permanent members, also voiced reservations about expanding the sanctions regime. Russian envoy Vasily Nebenzya acknowledged the threat posed by drone attacks but rejected what he described as an “equal responsibility” between the warring parties, arguing that the RSF was deliberately targeting civilians and infrastructure while the military was seeking to strike military targets. He also warned that further sanctions against Sudan would add to the economic pressure and ultimately fall on ordinary Sudanese. China’s Fu Cong likewise urged the council to be cautious about expanding sanctions, saying they should be “a means, not an end” and should not substitute for diplomatic efforts. He called for the existing measures to be implemented more effectively and “avoid arbitrary expansion of the severity and scope of the coercive measures, which might harm Sudan’s long-term peace, stability and unity, and disrupt the normal economic and social activities of its people and other countries.” With both Russia and China holding veto power, their opposition puts a significant obstacle in the way of any US-backed resolution to expand the embargo, unless Washington can find a compromise. Monday’s session marked a shift in the international conversation on Sudan, from general calls to end the war and protect civilians toward a search for more direct tools to disrupt the military structures sustaining the war. The UN briefings during the session exposed a widening gap between the pace of diplomatic engagement and the pace of the crisis on the ground, a Sudanese diplomatic source informed of the Security Council’s deliberations told Mada Masr. “The humanitarian catastrophe is moving faster than the international community’s capacity to respond to it,” they said. Continued fighting, drone strikes and the destruction of infrastructure are steadily narrowing civilians’ access to food, water and healthcare, while aid organizations face increasing obstacles in reaching those affected. According to the source, the consequences are likely to outlast the war itself, with lasting damage on Sudan’s economy, infrastructure, demographics and public services. The discussion, however, exposed “a clear split within the council over how to handle the war in Sudan,” the source said. “The disagreement is not just about sanctions,” the source explained, “but extends to how the nature of the war itself, and responsibility for it, is defined, as well as to the balance between protecting civilians and respecting state sovereignty.” With the US, France and Denmark on one side and Sudan, Russia and China on the other, any new move within the council will require understandings among the major powers, especially given the persistent divergence between Washington, Moscow and Beijing, the source said. The session ended without a new binding resolution, but it opened the way for negotiations over whether and how the proposal could advance. “The next battle inside the council will revolve around the language of the resolution, the scope of the embargo and the mechanisms for enforcing it,” the source said. The meeting’s significance lies less in an immediate decision than in the direction of the debate, according to the source. Weapons, foreign backing and drones are becoming more central to the international response to Sudan, as the council considers how to constrain the flows of arms, financing and military technology sustaining the war. That track, the source added, will remain intertwined with parallel efforts to secure a ceasefire, protect civilians and maintain humanitarian access. *** Khartoum prepares for UN General Assembly Sudan is preparing to use the UN General Assembly in New York in September to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture, with the government looking beyond the immediate management of the war toward the political and institutional order it wants to shape itself in a post-war period, according to diplomatic, government and political sources informed of the preparations. Burhan is expected to lead the delegation, but his inclusion is complicated by US sanctions, prompting the government to consider senior officials who could represent Sudan without constraining the bilateral and regional diplomacy it hopes to pursue on the sidelines. A government committee working on UN affairs has been consolidating Sudan’s position ahead of the meetings, with officials seeking to present a single line on the war and state sovereignty, relations with the UN, the government’s proposed internal political dialogue and the transition from humanitarian response to reconstruction, a Sudanese diplomatic source informed of preparations told Mada Masr. On the war, Khartoum plans to reassert its longstanding position that political negotiations must follow security arrangements, including the RSF’s withdrawal from civilian areas. The government also intends to push for international pressure on parties supporting the RSF with weapons and financing, framing the war as a question of preserving the state and its institutions, according to a Foreign Ministry source and a political source. The Foreign Ministry source expects scrutiny over aid access, civilian protection and humanitarian corridors, but said Khartoum is preparing to tie its position to sovereignty and government oversight of international operations. At the same time, officials want to shift the international aid discussion toward reconstruction, the return of displaced people and refugees, rebuilding public services and reviving the economy, a government source said. Two diplomatic sources said Khartoum is reassessing the future relationship with UN agencies and any international arrangements that could be proposed for the post-war period, after the UN Integrated Transition Assistance Mission in Sudan was terminated in 2024 The government is also preparing to make its internal political dialogue now being hurried in Khartoum part of its diplomatic pitch in New York, presenting it as a nationally owned process in which international actors would support and facilitate rather than shape its agenda or outcomes. But a political source close to the dialogue file said New York will also test the international response to a dialogue whose current, state-curated formulation is rejected by some civilian forces. Khartoum, the source said, is keen to be seen as broadening participation, even as it keeps its positions on the state, its unity and its institutions firmly off the table. The main complication for now is Burhan’s attendance. Although he is listed provisionally as a General Assembly speaker, the US Treasury sanctioned him in January 2025. A Foreign Ministry source stressed that the sanctions do not amount to a UN travel ban, but acknowledged that his entry into the US and his participation in bilateral meetings on the sidelines would require US legal and diplomatic arrangements. That has put alternative representation on the table. Two political sources informed of the preparations said Prime Minister Kamel Idris or Foreign Minister Mohie Eddin Salem could lead the delegation if Burhan cannot attend. The choice is about diplomatic utility: Burhan would give the Sudanese position greater political weight, while a delegation led by Idris or another senior official could conduct bilateral meetings without making the sanctions issue the defining feature of the visit. Regional diplomacy will run alongside the General Assembly agenda, with planned contacts involving Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt, African states and other actors involved in the Sudan file, a diplomatic source said. Those meetings would fit in a broader effort by Khartoum to rebuild its external relationships and expand its room for maneuver beyond traditional mediation channels. *** Political forces reject Khartoum dialogue Meeting of Sudanese political and civilian forces in Addis Ababa, August 23. Courtesy: The National Umma Party on Facebook Sudanese political and civilian forces opposed to the war rejected Burhan’s call for an internal dialogue, arguing that a political process launched while fighting continues and control of the country remains divided would reflect the wartime balance of power rather than help end the war. The collective rejection came at the conclusion of consultative meetings in Addis Ababa on Saturday and Sunday involving the Declaration of Principles Forces, the Sumud coalition, the National Umma Party, civil society organizations, women’s and youth networks and independent public figures. Representatives of the Islamist Popular Congress Party also took part. Mohamed al-Fekki, a leading figure in Sumud, told Mada Masr that the proposed dialogue would not end the war and could instead produce new political alignments that deepen fragmentation. “This is not a negotiating position or an attempt to raise the ceiling of demands. We are not at the stage of negotiating with the Port Sudan authority,” he said. The proposed dialogue, he added, treats the crisis as a separate political problem, while a settlement requires bringing civilian and armed actors into a process built first around ending the war. Fekki stressed that a dialogue held under the control of the military authorities running the venue faces fundamental questions over independence. Sumud has instead proposed a framework that links three tracks: ending the war, addressing the humanitarian crisis and pursuing a political process, he said. That political process should include Sudan’s main civilian constituencies, including anti-war forces and civilians aligned with either the military or the RSF, while excluding the former ruling National Congress Party and the Islamist current, he added. Sumud, however, has been in discussion with Saudi officials over a possible political role. A source in the coalition told Mada Masr in July that the Saudis have stepped up consultations to explore a political formula capable of bridging the gap between civilian forces and the military. The discussions, according to the source, have centered on designing a transition that the armed forces could accept while preserving civilian participation in governing the post-war period. Last week, Burhan offered temporary immunity to participants in the dialogue, including suspending criminal proceedings against those facing charges while taking part. The measure is meant to clear a legal hurdle for several Sumud leaders, including its head former Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok, who were charged over what the military saw as their proximity to the RSF during the coalition’s earlier iteration as part of the Civil Front for Democracy. According to a political source informed of the positions of the civilian forces, the central problem with Burhan’s invitation is its timing. Fighting continues in Kordofan, Darfur and elsewhere, while territorial control is divided among the military, the RSF, armed movements and local forces. The opposing civilian groups fear that any political process launched before addressing those realities would end up negotiating the consequences of the war rather than addressing its causes, the source said. A political source close to the government said the rejection by Sumud and its allies does not mean the initiative has failed. According to the source, Burhan has offered “broad guarantees on participation, protection and political freedoms,” while leaving a “national mechanism” to determine the participants and agenda. The source added that the government is betting that other political and social forces can still be brought into the process. *** Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here . El colapso de un glaciar y una gigantesca riada: qué sabemos de la tragedia de Nepal y qué falta por aclarar
items.description: A medida que pasan las horas tras la monstruosa riada del Tíbet y Nepal vamos conociendo más datos de cómo pudo producirse. A las 8.37 de la mañana del miércoles (4.52 en la España peninsular), los sismógrafos detectaron una fuerte señal en el Himalaya. En un primer momento, el Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos la identificó como un terremoto de magnitud 4,4, pero después la reclasificó como el rastro sísmico de un gigantesco deslizamiento de 5,2 provocado, según las investigaciones preliminares, por el colapso de un glaciar. Ese colapso ocurrió en una zona muy remota, por lo que será necesario analizar las imágenes por satélite para confirmar todos los datos. En cualquier caso, este fenómeno produjo una espectacular riada en el corredor montañoso de Gyirong, fronterizo entre Nepal y Tíbet, que ha causado ya más de 300 muertos y alrededor de 1.400 desaparecidos (el Ministerio de Exteriores confirma que no se ha podido localizar a cuatro españoles). Recopilamos lo que se sabe y lo que no sobre este desastre natural. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Effective coordination key to fighting galamsey – Zanetor
items.description: Environment, Science and Technology Minister-designate, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has identified effective coordination among relevant stakeholders as crucial to tackling illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, in Ghana. Speaking during her vetting before Parliament’s Appointments Committee on Thursday, 27 August, she said the fight against illegal mining required a coordinated approach involving all responsible institutions and partners. “I do believe that the easiest way to address it (Galamsey) is to have effective coordination between the ministries, departments and the agencies,” she said as an answer to a question on how she would help curb the illegal mining in the country when approved as minister for Environment, Science and Technology. “All of these activities (galamsey) are happening within our local governance space, and we have the decentralised Environmental Protection Authority and all these agencies at the local level as well. The regular reporting improves transparency, it also helps us to track the extent of interventions that are making an impact,” she added. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings pledged to prioritise engagements with the relevant stakeholders if approved by Parliament, with the aim of strengthening coordination and combining efforts to combat the menace. “To start with, I would want to sit with the relevant ministers of the various ministries that have an interest in the galamsey fight. This will range from the land as well as the local government to ensure that we are page to avoid the silo effect, and so that is what I will start with,” she noted. She said effective coordination would help align the work of the various institutions involved and create a united front against illegal mining and its damaging environmental consequences.

items.title: Ouagadougou : La BMCRF vend du riz à 10 000 F CFA le sac de 25 kg et à 20 000 F CFA celui de 50 kg
items.description: La Brigade Mobile de Contrôle économique et de la Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF) organise une vente exceptionnelle de cent tonnes de riz, saisies et confisquées pour stockage clandestin. Cette opération, ouverte par souscription préalable à compter du 1er septembre 2026, permettra aux populations d'acquérir ce produit à des prix sociaux. Les recettes générées seront intégralement reversées au Fonds de Soutien Patriotique (FSP). Cette initiative fait suite à une vaste opération de contrôle menée par la BMCRF, en collaboration avec l'Agence Burkinabè de Normalisation, de la Métrologie et de la Qualité (ABNORM), le mercredi 19 août 2026 dans plusieurs quartiers de Ouagadougou. Les équipes mixtes ont alors découvert environ 100 tonnes de riz entreposées dans une habitation transformée en lieu de stockage clandestin. D'autres infractions ont été constatées, notamment la vente de produits de première nécessité au-delà des prix réglementaires, le reconditionnement frauduleux de riz dans des sacs douteux, ainsi que la mise en vente de nombreux produits périmés. Face à ces dérives, plusieurs boutiques et magasins ont été scellés et les commerçants fautifs soumis à des sanctions, dont des amendes et des travaux d'intérêt général. Conformément à la réglementation sur la fixation des prix et des marges bénéficiaires des produits de grande consommation, la BMCRF procède désormais à la vente à prix social de la marchandise saisie. Les personnes intéressées peuvent participer à cette opération par souscription préalable auprès de la BMCRF, sise en face de l'ex-Primature. Les souscriptions sont ouvertes à compter du mardi 1er septembre 2026, de 09 heures à 15 heures, et ce, jusqu'à épuisement du stock . Les postulants doivent se munir de leurs documents d'identité valides. Les détails des prix par catégorie de riz sont précisés dans un tableau annexé au communiqué officiel. Les ressources issues de cette vente seront intégralement reversées au Fonds de Soutien Patriotique (FSP). La BMCRF annonce par ailleurs la poursuite des contrôles sur l'ensemble du territoire national et invite la population à dénoncer tout cas suspect via les numéros verts suivants : 80 00 11 84, 80 00 11 85 et 80 00 11 86. Lire aussi : Non-respect des prix des produits : Le ministre Poda surprend des commerçants « véreux » à Ouaga Minute.bf

items.title: En prétendant renommer le lac Ontario, Trump s’inscrit dans la lignée de Mobutu
items.description: Le 25 août, Donald Trump a annoncé sur son réseau social Truth Social que les États-Unis envisageaient « sérieusement » de rebaptiser le lac Ontario « lac Amérique », en pleine guerre commerciale avec le Canada, et après ses provocations et ses nombreuses déclarations visant à faire du pays le « 51e État ». Aujourd’hui, jeudi 27, un compte officiel de la Maison-Blanche a diffusé une vidéo devenue virale sur TikTok. pic.twitter.com/ykuNEYi7PY — Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) August 27, 2026 On y voit le président, derrière son bureau à la Maison-Blanche, barrer le nom « Lake Ontario » sur une carte et écrire « Lake America » à la place, à l'aide d'un feutre. Le nom « Ontario » est d'origine iroquoise, et existait avant la formation du Canada et des États-Unis. Dérivé du mot iroquois Ontarí:io , qui signifie « beau lac » ou « lac aux eaux scintillantes », il est attesté sur les cartes européennes dès le XVIIe siècle. L’ancien gouverneur de la Nouvelle-France, Champlain, le nomme « lac Saint-Louis » en 1632, tandis que la cartographie française de la fin du XVIIe siècle l'appelle « lac Frontenac », en référence à un gouverneur du territoire. Ce n’est pas la première fois que le président américain cible la toponymie amérindienne, Donald Trump a par exemple rendu par décret au mont Denali le nom de « mont McKinley ». Il se concentre ces jours-ci sur le toponyme Ontario pour viser le Premier ministre de la province, Doug Ford, qui avait diffusé en octobre 2025 une publicité contre les droits de douane utilisant la voix de Ronald Reagan. La toponymie au niveau fédéral relève de la compétence de l'U.S. Board on Geographic Names, sommé de se conformer par décret. Dans le cas d'un lac situé sur un territoire commun aux États-Unis et au Canada, l'accord de 1987 entre ces deux pays sur la coordination des noms de lieux privilégie les « noms officiels établis » International boundary names : United States of America, Canada and Mexico , Cinquième conférence des Nations Unies sur la standardisation des noms géographiques, 18-31 août 1987.'> 1 . Le gouvernement canadien a déjà répliqué : « Nous l'appellerons toujours le lac Ontario » Transcription de l’entretien avec la ministre de l’industrie du Canada, Mélanie Joly , CNN , 25 août 2026.'> 2 . Ce n’est pas la première fois que Donald Trump décide unilatéralement de renommer une entité géographique. Le cas le plus récent est le décret qu'il a promulgué le 20 janvier 2025, par lequel il a rebaptisé le golfe du Mexique « golfe d'Amérique ». Cette décision n'est juridiquement contraignante que pour les agences fédérales américaines, mais elle a été adoptée par plusieurs cartes numériques américaines, notamment par la plus influente d’entre elles, Google Maps. De son côté, l’Associated Press s'est vu interdire l'accès au Bureau ovale pour avoir maintenu le nom « golfe du Mexique » dans ses consignes. Les précédents de changements unilatéraux de toponymie de lacs sont rares, et sont souvent liés à des dictatures de l'époque des indépendances. Ces modifications survivent rarement à la disgrâce ou à la mort de leur instigateur. En 1973, « le président à vie » ougandais Idi Amin Dada rebaptise ainsi le lac Édouard « lac Idi Amin Dada », tandis que le président de la République démocratique du Congo, Mobutu, renomme le lac Albert « lac Mobutu Sese Seko ». Dans les années 1930, la dynastie Pahlavi en Iran avait rebaptisé le lac d'Urmia « lac Razaya » (lac de Reza) en l'honneur de Reza Shah, mais ce nom a été aboli avant même la Révolution islamique de 1979. L’article En prétendant renommer le lac Ontario, Trump s’inscrit dans la lignée de Mobutu est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Kuje Chairman’s comment: No effort to hold Shekwolo to account — Amnesty
items.description: ABUJA — Amnesty International Nigeria has criticised the alleged failure of security agencies to hold the Chairman of Kuje Area Council of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Samuel Danjuma Shekwolo, to account over comments allegedly threatening violence against residents who refuse to vote for the All Progressives Congress, APC. The human rights organisation made the allegation in a post on its X platform, expressing concern over what it described as a climate of fear among residents of the area council. According to Amnesty, Shekwolo’s alleged attempt to make voting for the APC a condition for residents to live peacefully and exercise their civic rights was unlawful. “Residents of Kuje Area Council FCT will continue to live in fear as no effort has been made by security agencies to hold the council chairman Samuel Danjuma Shekwolo to account, for threatening to unleash violence on anybody who would not vote for APC,” Amnesty said. The organisation said such alleged threats could undermine citizens’ rights to freely participate in elections and choose candidates or political parties of their choice. It called on Nigerian authorities to ensure that politicians and other leaders who carry out, incite or threaten politically, religiously or ethnically motivated violence or other human rights abuses are held accountable. “Ahead of 2027 elections and beyond, it is essential that the Nigerian authorities ensure that any politician or other leaders, of any political party or grouping, responsible for carrying out or inciting or threatening politically, religiously or ethnically-motivated violence or human rights abuses must be held to account,” it said. The allegation comes as political parties and politicians intensify preparations for the 2027 general elections. Kuje is one of the six area councils in the FCT, where residents will participate in the forthcoming electoral process. The Nigerian Constitution and electoral laws guarantee citizens the right to vote and participate in elections freely and without intimidation or coercion. Political threats and violence have remained major concerns during Nigeria’s electoral cycles, prompting repeated calls for security agencies to protect voters and ensure that citizens can exercise their franchise without fear. Amnesty International’s statement has consequently renewed attention on the need for authorities to investigate allegations of political intimidation and take appropriate action where wrongdoing is established. The allegation against Shekwolo has not been independently established from the information available, and his response was not included in Amnesty International Nigeria’s statement provided for this report. The post Kuje Chairman’s comment: No effort to hold Shekwolo to account — Amnesty appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: El violento secuestro del camionero que perdió media tonelada de cocaína
items.description: Más de media tonelada de cocaína que desaparece. Un clan albanés de narcotráfico que quiere recuperar su mercancía al precio que sea. Varios transportistas de origen rumano que se pasan unos a otros el encargo de llevar la droga por Europa y que luego, cuando el alijo es robado, se echan la culpa mutuamente de la pérdida. Y un vídeo de unos pocos segundos que empieza a circular por los teléfonos móviles en el que un individuo apunta a otro con una pistola en la cabeza mientras le grita: “¿Dónde está lo nuestro? ¿Dónde está la mierda?“. La Policía Nacional logró liberar el pasado 10 de julio al hombre de 47 años que aparecía en esas imágenes amenazado por un arma de fuego, según ha informado este jueves el Ministerio del Interior. Llevaba más de una semana secuestrado y, tras haber sufrido numerosas palizas , estaba siendo trasladado a un lugar apartado de la provincia de Barcelona, supuestamente para ser ejecutado. En el operativo fue detenido uno de los presuntos captores que, en el momento de su arresto, llevaba una pistola Tokarev , de origen ruso, que intentó usar contra los agentes. La cocaína no ha aparecido. Tampoco el resto de los protagonistas de esta historia de droga y venganza. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un milliardaire américain reconnaît avoir utilisé l'IA pour critiquer la politique du Trésor américain
items.description: Le milliardaire et investisseur americain, Stanley Druckenmiller, a reconnu avoir eu recours a l'intelligence artificielle pour preparer une tribune critiquant la politique du Tresor americain face a l'alourdissement de la dette publique, rapporte le 25 août The Wall Street Journal . Interroge sur les conditions dans lesquelles le texte avait ete redige, l'investisseur de 73 ans n'a pas cherche a dissimuler l'utilisation de ces outils. Il a notamment fait valoir qu'il avait toujours ete plus a l'aise avec l'economie qu'avec l'ecriture, tout en insistant sur le fait que les idees developpees dans la tribune etaient bien les siennes et qu'il les defendait depuis plus de 15 ans : « J'avais un B en anglais, mais un A+ en economie. Ce sont mes idees et j'en parle depuis plus de 15 ans, comme le savent tous ceux qui me connaissent. Aurais-je prefere devenir un excellent ecrivain ? Oui, mais ce n'est pas ce que je suis ». Druckenmiller a egalement precise que lui et ses collegues utilisaient les principaux outils d'intelligence artificielle, parmi lesquels Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini et Perplexity, notamment pour preparer des textes. Il a compare leur utilisation a l'aide que peut apporter un redacteur de discours ou une calculatrice. « a 73 ans, je suis plutot fier de les utiliser », a-t-il fait savoir. Son recours a l'IA a commence a susciter des interrogations apres que des utilisateurs des reseaux sociaux avaient soumis sa tribune a des logiciels destines a reperer les textes generes artificiellement. Au-dela de cette controverse, le texte, intitule « Let the Bond Market Speak » (« ecoutons ce que dit le marche obligataire »), porte avant tout sur la trajectoire des finances publiques americaines et la maniere dont le Tresor tente de repondre aux tensions sur le marche obligataire. Druckenmiller conteste en particulier la decision de doubler le volume des rachats de titres de dette a long terme, de 2 milliards de dollars a au moins 4 milliards par operation, annoncee apres que le rendement des obligations du Tresor a 30 ans a atteint son plus haut niveau depuis 19 ans. Un avertissement que Washington ne devrait pas ignorer Pour l'investisseur, la decision du Tresor d'augmenter ses rachats d'obligations revient a agir sur les symptomes plutot que sur les causes. En cherchant ainsi a contenir la hausse des rendements, le departement tentait, selon lui, d'attenuer un signal que le marche adressait precisement aux autorites americaines sur l'etat des finances publiques. Druckenmiller appuie son raisonnement sur plusieurs indicateurs : un deficit budgetaire qui avoisine 6 % du PIB, une inflation toujours superieure a l'objectif fixe par la Reserve federale et une dette publique qui depasse desormais 40 000 milliards de dollars. Dans ces conditions, etouffer le message envoye par le marche obligataire ne ferait, selon lui, que repousser les ajustements necessaires. Washington pourrait ainsi differer la reduction du deficit, mais au prix d'un probleme de dette encore plus difficile et plus douloureux a resoudre par la suite. Stanley Druckenmiller dispose d'une fortune estimee a 7,8 milliards de dollars par Forbes , ce qui le place au 505e rang des personnes les plus riches au monde.

items.title: Ukraine : les organes anticorruption, un «gouvernement parallèle» qui ébranle Zelensky
items.description: Les institutions chargees de lutter contre la corruption en Ukraine ont acquis une telle influence qu'elles fonctionnent desormais comme un veritable contre-pouvoir face a l'executif, rapporte The Economist le 24 août , qui va jusqu'a les decrire comme un « gouvernement parallele », alors que plusieurs enquetes touchent des responsables situes au plus pres du pouvoir. Cette montee en puissance est notamment apparue au grand jour le 19 août, avec la publication d'enregistrements de conversations telephoniques obtenues dans le cadre d'enquetes anticorruption. Parmi les personnes citees figure Iryna Moudra, qui occupait jusqu'alors le poste de cheffe adjointe de l'administration presidentielle. Selon The Economist , le Bureau national anticorruption d'Ukraine (NABU), le Parquet specialise dans la lutte contre la corruption (SAPO) et la Haute Cour anticorruption ont progressivement acquis une autonomie leur permettant de peser directement sur le fonctionnement du pouvoir. Les conversations rendues publiques revelent notamment que de hauts responsables ont cherche a garder la lutte contre la corruption sous controle. Les enquetes menees par ces institutions provoquent desormais un reel malaise au sein de l'administration de Volodymyr Zelensky. Les tensions avec le pouvoir ne sont d'ailleurs pas nouvelles. En 2025, Zelensky avait soutenu des modifications visant a placer le NABU et le SAPO sous l'autorite de structures davantage controlees par l'etat. Cette tentative avait provoque des manifestations et contraint le « president ukrainien » a revenir sur sa position. Les evenements du mois d'août illustrent la persistance des tensions entre le pouvoir et les institutions anticorruption. Le 19 août, Volodymyr Zelensky a limoge Iryna Moudra de son poste au sein de l'administration presidentielle. Des perquisitions ont ensuite ete menees a son domicile. Le meme jour, le NABU et le SAPO ont annonce l'operation « Forrest Gump », destinee a demanteler une organisation criminelle qui aurait ete dirigee par un depute en exercice et un ancien membre de la Rada. Selon les enqueteurs, des responsables de l'administration presidentielle, du ministere de la Justice et de Sense Bank auraient ete impliques dans ce reseau, parmi lesquels Iryna Moudra. L'ancienne responsable de l'administration presidentielle a ete arretee le 25 août. Bruxelles attend toujours des reformes anticorruption Dans le meme temps, l'Ukraine peine a mettre en œuvre les reformes exigees par l'Union europeenne dans les domaines de la justice et de la lutte contre la corruption. Le 25 août, le quotidien allemand Süddeutsche Zeitung a estime que l'Ukraine n'avait pratiquement pas avance dans la realisation des changements necessaires dans les domaines de la justice et de la lutte contre la corruption, dont depend la poursuite d'une partie de l'aide financiere europeenne. L'accord avec Bruxelles prevoit en effet le versement de plusieurs milliards d'euros supplementaires a condition que Kiev poursuive ses efforts contre la corruption. Or, selon le journal allemand, les reformes sont aujourd'hui au point mort. Parmi les mesures considerees comme urgentes par l'Union europeenne figurent notamment l'elargissement des pouvoirs du NABU et du SAPO, le renforcement de l'independance du Parquet general et du Bureau national d'enquete, ainsi que la suppression des dispositions qui compliquent les enquetes dans les affaires de corruption.

items.title: Tanzania ruling party expels Vice President after historic resignation
items.description: Tanzania’s ruling party has expelled the country’s vice president just days after his historic resignation. This rapid escalation tests the democratic credentials and political stability of the East African nation. Analysts view the ouster as a stark indicator of deep fractures within the dominant political establishment. Party Disciplines Resigning Official The Chama Cha Mapinduzi party took decisive disciplinary action against Emmanuel Nchimbi. Leaders announced his expulsion due to alleged indiscipline following his sudden decision to leave office. He served for ten months before making his exit. Observers note this marks an unprecedented moment in the modern history of the country. Controversial Statements Spark Friction The fifty-four-year-old official recently made public remarks that drew intense scrutiny. He urged citizens to “fight for a new constitution”. Observers interpreted this call as a direct challenge to the administration. This stance signalled major political fallout with President Samia Suluhu Hassan. He also shared his brief resignation letter on his Instagram account on Tuesday morning. He stated that he would retire from public life because he had “become convinced, without doubt, that the president wants changes”. He noted his departure would take effect at the end of next week, adding that he would remain “a good citizen”. Contested Election and Deadly Unrest The political crisis traces back to the disputed presidential vote held last October. The incumbent administration secured a landslide victory in an election boycotted by major opposition groups. The main opposition faction, Chadema, had demanded electoral reforms prior to participation. Post-election demonstrations met with a severe state response. Human rights organizations accused security forces of utilizing excessive force. An official inquiry later revealed that at least five hundred people died during the unrest. The head of the investigative commission reported that the actual death toll was likely higher. He explained that many families buried relatives without registering the bodies at morgues. The inquiry recommended investigating the use of firearms after witnesses reported troops shooting people inside homes. Succession Plans and Institutional Control The ruling party quickly moved to fill the vacant seat. Officials nominated Energy Minister Deogratius Ndejembi to assume the role. Parliament must now approve his nomination. The ruling party has maintained continuous power since independence from Britain in 1961. The organisation remains deeply intertwined with state apparatuses and security institutions. Past transitions followed predictable patterns under the dominant political framework. The sudden departure of a sitting deputy leader shatters the traditional image of internal harmony. Observers wait to see if the administration can restore confidence amid rising public dissent. Balancing institutional continuity with genuine political reform remains the central challenge for Tanzania as leadership navigates this unprecedented transition.

items.title: Incendies tragiques : Tebboune décrète un deuil national
items.description: Suite aux décès de plusieurs citoyens dans les incendies qui se sont déclarés dans certaines wilayas du centre et de l'Est du pays mercredi, le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a décrété ce jeudi 27 août un deuil national. Mercredi 26 août, des incendies se sont déclarés dans plusieurs localités du Nord du pays, faisant au moins 12 morts, dont un garçon de huit ans, à Béjaïa, Jijel et Tizi-Ouzou. Le premier bilan annoncé mercredi soir par le ministre de l’Intérieur, Saïd Sayoud, fait état de cinq décès à Jijel, quatre à Béjaïa et trois à Tizi-Ouzou. Pas moins de 54 personnes ont été blessées, dont « six dans un état grave ». « Je décrète un deuil national de trois jours, avec mise en berne de l’emblème national » Suite à ce drame, le président de la République a adressé un message de condoléances aux familles des victimes et a décrété un deuil national de trois jours, à compter de ce jeudi 27 août, indique un communiqué de la présidence de la République. « C’est une période difficile que nous traversons tous, où les flammes ont pris nos concitoyens par surprise alors même que nous avions commencé à indemniser les sinistrés des précédents incendies qui avaient été maîtrisés », indique le chef de l’État dans son message. « Face à cette terrible épreuve, je ne peux que m’incliner en hommage aux âmes de nos concitoyens que nous avons perdus dans cette tragédie (…) J’adresse également mes condoléances les plus sincères à toutes les familles endeuillées par cette tragédie », ajoute-t-il. Suite à cette douloureuse épreuve, « je décrète un deuil national de trois jours, avec mise en berne de l’emblème national sur l'ensemble du territoire national, et annulation de toutes les manifestations festives et compétitions sportives nationales », lit-on encore dans le message du président de la République. La première journée du championnat professionnel de Ligue 1 Mobilis reportée Dans le même sillage, la Ligue de football algérienne (LFP) a annoncé dans un communiqué le report du lancement du championnat de Ligue 1 Mobilis 2026/2027, alors que le coup d’envoi est prévu initialement ce jeudi 27 août. Ce report intervient après la décision du président Abdelmadjid Tebboune de décréter trois jours de deuil national et d’annuler toutes les compétitions sportives nationales. « Compte tenu de la proclamation du deuil national, la Ligue annonce le report de la première journée du championnat professionnel à la semaine prochaine, les 3, 4 et 5 septembre 2026 », indique l’instance dans son communiqué. La Ligue précise que les dates de reprise des compétitions et le nouveau calendrier des matchs reportés seront communiqués ultérieurement, tout en réitérant « sa solidarité totale avec les familles des victimes et les personnes touchées, et souhaitant un prompt rétablissement à tous les blessés ». L’article Incendies tragiques : Tebboune décrète un deuil national est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Gov’t must fund CSIR to develop biological plastic alternatives – Zanetor
items.description: Minister-designate for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has called on the government to channel funding to the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) to develop locally produced alternatives to plastic. Appearing before Parliament’s Appointments Committee on Thursday, August 27, she said Ghana’s efforts to tackle the growing plastic waste crisis should go beyond bans and restrictions to include investment in research into environmentally friendly substitutes. According to her, the CSIR is well positioned to research and develop biological alternatives using locally available agricultural products such as cassava and hemp. “I believe that there’s a policy on plastic waste that we have as a country, and that is supposed to encompass how we plan to address this. “What I believe can be done in addition to this is to channel some funding towards the CSIR, the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, so that they can actually look into biological alternatives,” she said. She cited cassava and hemp among the plant-based materials that could be explored in producing alternatives to conventional plastics. “We have a lot of plant produce that can be used to make plastic alternatives which can break down and don’t actually persevere in the environment,” she added. Her proposal forms part of a broader call for Ghana to combine policy interventions, research and innovation in addressing the country’s persistent plastic waste challenge as the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) has announced that Ghana will officially ban the production, importation, distribution, sale and use of polystyrene foam products, commonly known as Styrofoam or takeaway packs, from January 1, 2027. The ban is part of a broader national strategy to tackle plastic pollution, improve environmental sanitation, and promote sustainable consumption practices across the country.

items.title: Alleged 9/11 mastermind to go on trial in June 2028
items.description: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the alleged mastermind of the September 11, 2001 attacks on the United States, will go on trial before a US military court in June 2028, an official said Thursday. A spokesman for the US military court at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, where Mohammed is incarcerated, said the trial would begin on June 5, 2028. Mohammed, also known as "KSM," was considered one of Al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden's top lieutenants before he was captured in March 2003 in Pakistan.

items.title: Anger in Upper West over Dr Pelpuo reshuffle; residents demand cabinet slot
items.description: The reshuffle announced by President John Dramani Mahama on Wednesday has hit the Upper West Region like a bombshell. Dr Rashid Hassan Pelpuo, who was serving as Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment, has been moved to the Presidency as Minister of State in charge of Special Initiatives. In Wa and across the region, traders, tricycle riders, youth groups and NDC supporters who spoke to JoyNews expressed disappointment and anger, calling on the President to rescind the decision. For many young people, their hopes of securing employment were tied to Dr Pelpuo’s presence at the Labour Ministry. “Our livelihood and survival depend on Dr. Pelpuo,’’ tricycle operator Ahmed Jimba fumes. Moving him from that ministry will truncate our dreams of getting employment,” trader Vida Dabagah said. Others argue that the new portfolio – Special Initiatives at the Presidency – is little known to them and will bring little direct benefit to the region. Beyond Dr Pelpuo, residents are raising a bigger concern: With a population of over 900,000, the Upper West Region currently has no Cabinet-level representation. They are appealing to the President to either reverse the reshuffle or appoint an Upper Westerner to Cabinet. The political spin is already gaining momentum. Supporters of the opposition NPP have questioned the NDC government’s loyalty to the region, despite the region giving the NDC a clean sweep of all 11 parliamentary seats in the 2024 elections. They contrast this with the NPP era, when despite winning 5 seats in 2016 and 3 seats in 2020, the region was still rewarded with a substantive Cabinet Minister and a Deputy. On social media, many have taken to chastising the government, asking whether the Upper West has “sold their dog for a monkey” – or in simple terms, traded their colour television for a black-and-white TV.

items.title: Gusau confirms resignation as NFF president
items.description: ABUJA — President of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), Alhaji Ibrahim Gusau, has confirmed his resignation from office, bringing his tenure as the head of the country’s football governing body to an end. Gusau officially announced his resignation on Thursday at a press conference in Abuja, amid mounting pressure over the recent fortunes of Nigeria’s national teams. His announcement followed reports that he and members of the NFF Executive Committee had resigned from their positions. The development comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over Nigeria’s poor performances in international football. The Super Eagles failed to qualify for the 2022 and 2026 FIFA World Cups, while the Super Falcons recently suffered a major setback by failing to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. Nigeria’s age-grade teams have also endured disappointing results, with the Golden Eaglets failing to qualify for the FIFA U-17 World Cup for three consecutive editions despite being the most successful team in the history of the competition, with five titles. The country’s Olympic football team, the Dream Team, has similarly struggled to regain the prominence it enjoyed after winning the gold medal at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics. The string of setbacks had intensified calls from football stakeholders and supporters for changes in the administration of the game and a fresh approach to developing the national teams. Gusau’s resignation also comes amid an emergency meeting of the NFF Congress convened to deliberate on the crisis within the federation. The proposed agenda for the meeting includes the current developments within the NFF, the status and functioning of the Executive Committee and Secretariat, and the implications for the governance, stability and independence of the federation. The Congress is also expected to consider appropriate measures under the NFF, Confederation of African Football (CAF) and FIFA statutes before determining the way forward. Gusau’s resignation is expected to usher in a new phase for Nigerian football, with stakeholders likely to focus on stabilising the federation and rebuilding the country’s national teams. items.title: New airport projects to ease congestion, improve passenger experience—Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama says new developments being constructed at the Accra International Airport will ease congestion, improve traffic circulation, and make movement around the airport more convenient for passengers. He made the remarks on Thursday, August 27, at the sod-cutting ceremony for the Multi-Tiered, Multi-Purpose Car Park and Airport Hotels Complex. The seven-storey facility will provide about 2,030 covered parking bays, two hotels, a pedestrian sky-bridge linking directly to Terminal 3, a shopping mall, a food court, retail and office spaces, as well as a sky lounge and observatory. According to President Mahama, the development would provide additional parking, improve traffic flow and make better use of the airport’s limited land. “It will provide additional parking; it will improve traffic circulation, it will reduce congestion and optimise the use of limited land within the airport enclave,” he said. He added that building vertically would allow the airport to use its space more efficiently while creating room for other services. Two hotels, commercial facilities The complex, he said, will include a 120-room five-star premium hotel providing accommodation options at different price points. It will also feature restaurants, shopping facilities, banking and travel services, a food court, and office spaces for corporate users. President Mahama said the development would create new commercial opportunities and support business activities within the airport environment. Digital parking system President Mahama said technology would be central to the project, with the parking system incorporating automatic number plate recognition and operating on a cashless, ticketless basis. Parking guidance systems, electric vehicle charging points, and centralised CCTV surveillance will also be provided. He said the systems would improve traffic management, strengthen security, and reduce delays. “These systems will improve traffic management, strengthen security, reduce delays and make the entire parking experience more seamless,” he said. President Mahama said the mix of parking, accommodation, retail, dining, and business facilities would transform the airport enclave into a more vibrant economic space. “This thoughtful mix of parking, accommodation, retail, dining, and business services will improve the convenience and help transform the airport enclave into a more vibrant economic space,” he said. He added that the project would support longer transit stays and help consolidate the Accra International Airport’s operations as a 24-hour facility. “Indeed, this development will consolidate the Accra International Airport’s operation as a true 24-hour facility,” he said. President Mahama also welcomed efforts by the Ghana Airports Company Limited, the Civil Aviation Authority, and other institutions operating at the airport to clamp down on soliciting and begging for tips from visitors.

items.title: Court orders NDLEA to produce KayCee Luxury
items.description: By Henry Ojelu A Federal High Court sitting in Lagos has ordered the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, to produce socialite Afolabi Kazeem Micheal, popularly known as ‘KayCee Luxury’, before the court over his continued detention without formal arraignment. The order followed an ex parte application filed by Afolabi through his counsel, A. Labi-Lawal, SAN, pursuant to the Fundamental Rights (Enforcement Procedure) Rules, 2009. Afolabi was arrested by operatives of the NDLEA on August 13 at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, while preparing to travel to Paris. His legal team approached the court after he had spent more than 14 days in custody without, according to the application, being formally charged or arraigned. The applicant is asking the court to intervene in what he contends is a violation of his fundamental rights arising from his continued detention. The court, in response to the application, directed the NDLEA to produce Afolabi before it for the matter to be heard. items.title: Start waste segregation at household level – Zanetor
items.description: Minister-designate for Environment, Science, and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has called for the promotion of a culture of waste segregation at the household, school, and community levels to improve Ghana’s management of solid waste. She said separating waste at the source would make it easier to determine how different forms of waste should be treated, while also supporting efforts to produce compost and promote recycling. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings made the call when she appeared before Parliament’s Appointments Committee on Thursday, August 27, as part of her vetting. She said waste management required a combination of proper disposal systems, public education, stronger enforcement, and innovative approaches to the treatment and reuse of waste. “We need to also create a culture of segregation of waste in order to be able to know what’s going where,” she said. She explained that waste segregation should begin from the most basic units of society, including households, schools, and communities. “If we’re looking at the creation of compost, then from the household level, from the schools, from the very basic units of our communities, we should start the issue of segregation of waste,” she said. Landfills Dr Agyeman-Rawlings also called for greater attention to the design and management of landfills to prevent harmful substances from entering the soil and groundwater. She said landfills must have a non-permeable base before waste is deposited to prevent leaching. “One thing that ought to be done, and I would want to have greater insight into that, is that landfills must have a non-permeable base before items are dumped on it to prevent leaching into the soil and into the groundwater,” she said. She described the measure as an absolute necessity and said existing practices at e-waste collection points could provide a basis for extending similar safeguards to other waste management facilities. “This is something that has to be looked at as an absolute necessity. I do know that that is what’s practiced at a collection point for the e-waste, but I believe it needs to be extended,” she said. Alternative approaches to solid waste Beyond conventional waste disposal, the Minister-designate said Ghana could explore alternative methods of handling solid waste, including technologies that could turn waste into energy and other useful products. “There are countries that import solid waste in order to use for their thermal power generation,” she said. She also proposed the use of pyrolysis technology to process plastic waste into useful products such as fuel and cooking gas. “We can also look at pyrolysis of plastics, which can then be used to generate fuel and cooking gas,” she said. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings added that some types of plastic could also be recycled into reusable materials, creating opportunities to reduce the volume of plastic waste while making productive use of discarded materials. “Then there’s also, obviously, the recycling of some kinds of plastic into reusable materials,” she said. She said addressing Ghana’s waste management challenges would therefore require a broad approach rather than relying on a single solution.

items.title: Zanetor to resign as Pan-African Parliament Vice-President if approved as minister
items.description: Environment, Science and Technology Minister-designate, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, says she will resign from her position as Vice-President of the Pan-African Parliament if Parliament approves her ministerial nomination. She made the disclosure during her vetting before Parliament’s Appointments Committee on Thursday, 27 August. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings was responding to Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, who asked whether she had already resigned from the continental parliamentary body ahead of taking up the ministerial role. She explained that she would return to the Pan-African Parliament to formally relinquish the position after receiving parliamentary approval to serve as Ghana’s Minister for Environment, Science and Technology. “The procedure per the Pan-African Parliament is in the next section. I am to go back and formally hand in my resignation,” she said. “Particularly after being given a nod (as Minister for Environment, Science and Technology),” Chairman of the Vetting committee, Bernard Ahiafor added. Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings was elected second vice President of the Pan-African Parliament in April this year. At an election on Thursday, April 30, 2026, in South Africa, she got 131 votes as against 51 by her opponent. She joined Ghana’s delegation to the Pan-African Parliament in July 2025. The Pan-African Parliament, an organ of the African Union, plays a key role in promoting integration, cooperation and democratic governance among member states. The second vice president position is part of the Bureau (leadership) of the Pan-African Parliament, which includes a President and four Vice Presidents. As second vice president, she will be part of the bureau responsible for guiding the Parliament’s affairs and supporting its legislative and advisory functions. She will no longer play these roles when vetted and approved by Parliament for her new job.

items.title: Landfills must have non-permeable bases to prevent groundwater contamination – Zanetor
items.description: Minister-designate for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has called for the mandatory use of non-permeable bases at landfill sites to prevent contaminated liquid from seeping into the soil and groundwater. She said the measure is necessary to address the growing environmental and public health risks associated with leachate from landfill sites across the country. Leachate is the contaminated liquid generated when water passes through waste at landfill sites. If not properly contained, it can carry harmful chemicals and pollutants into surrounding soil and groundwater.
